```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# WHY this chunk: central config for every figure/table, artifact paths, and
# graceful capability detection (plotly/DT power the interactive views; static
# PNG/kable are the fallbacks so the report renders even without them).
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
have_plotly <- requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)
have_DT     <- requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)

outdir    <- params$outdir
cfg       <- params$cfg
p_qc      <- file.path(outdir, "qc", "qc_results.tsv")
p_varmeta <- file.path(outdir, "qc", "variance_vs_metadata.tsv")
p_pca_tsv <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "pca_scores.tsv")
p_pca_pv  <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "pca_percentvar.txt")
p_pca_bc_tsv <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "pca_scores_bc.tsv")
p_pca_bc_pv  <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "pca_percentvar_bc.txt")
p_pca     <- file.path(outdir, "plots", "pca.png")
p_pca_bc  <- file.path(outdir, "plots", "pca_batch_corrected.png")
p_vm_png  <- file.path(outdir, "plots", "variance_vs_metadata.png")
p_volcano <- file.path(outdir, "plots", "volcano.png")
p_de      <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "de_results.tsv")
p_ora     <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "enrichment_ora.tsv")
p_gsea    <- file.path(outdir, "tables", "enrichment_gsea.tsv")
p_dot     <- file.path(outdir, "plots", "enrichment_dotplot.png")

read_tsv_safe  <- function(p, ...) if (file.exists(p)) utils::read.delim(p, check.names = FALSE, ...) else NULL
img_tag <- function(p, alt = "") if (file.exists(p)) sprintf('<img src="%s" alt="%s" style="max-width:100%%;border-radius:8px;">\n', normalizePath(p), alt) else ""

# Build an interactive PCA scatter from a saved scores TSV. Shared by the main
# PCA and the batch-corrected PCA so both look and behave identically (hover =
# sample + group; color = tested factor; symbol = batch variable when present).
pca_plotly <- function(scores_tsv, pv_txt, static_png) {
  sc <- read_tsv_safe(scores_tsv)
  pv <- if (file.exists(pv_txt)) as.numeric(strsplit(readLines(pv_txt), "\t")[[1]]) else NULL
  color_by <- if (!is.null(cfg)) cfg$contrast[[1]] else NULL
  if (have_plotly && !is.null(sc) && all(c("PC1","PC2") %in% colnames(sc)) &&
      !is.null(color_by) && color_by %in% colnames(sc)) {
    hover <- sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>%s: %s", sc$sample, color_by, sc[[color_by]])
    args <- list(data = sc, x = ~PC1, y = ~PC2, type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
                 color = sc[[color_by]], text = hover, hoverinfo = "text",
                 marker = list(size = 13, line = list(width = 1, color = "#ffffff")))
    bv <- if (nzchar(params$batch_vars)) trimws(strsplit(params$batch_vars, ",")[[1]])[1] else NA
    if (!is.na(bv) && bv %in% colnames(sc)) args$symbol <- sc[[bv]]
    return(plotly::layout(do.call(plotly::plot_ly, args),
      xaxis = list(title = if (!is.null(pv)) sprintf("PC1: %s%% variance", pv[1]) else "PC1", zeroline = FALSE),
      yaxis = list(title = if (!is.null(pv)) sprintf("PC2: %s%% variance", pv[2]) else "PC2", zeroline = FALSE),
      legend = list(title = list(text = color_by))))
  }
  if (file.exists(static_png)) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(static_png)) else knitr::asis_output("_PCA not available._")
}

PAL <- list(up = "#e05252", down = "#3f7fbf", ns = "#c9ccd1",
            pass = "#2e9e5b", warn = "#e0a800", fail = "#d64545")
pca_ntop <- if (!is.null(cfg) && !is.null(cfg$explore$pca_ntop)) cfg$explore$pca_ntop else 500
```

```{css, echo=FALSE}
  --bg:#f6f8fb; --card:#ffffff; --ink:#1f2733; --muted:#5b6675; --line:#e4e8ef;
  --accent:#4f46e5; --accent2:#0ea5e9;

.legend span{ display:inline-block; margin-right:14px; }
.dot{ display:inline-block; width:10px; height:10px; border-radius:50%; margin-right:5px; vertical-align:middle; }
/* ---- DataTables (DT) widgets: make them follow the page theme ------------- */
```

# QC panel

The traffic-light panel is the run's quality gate. **Green = PASS**, **amber =
WARN** (proceed, but review), **red = FAIL** (would stop the run without
`--force`). Hover a check name for what it means.

```{r qc-panel, results='asis'}
qc <- read_tsv_safe(p_qc)
# Short "why" tooltips for each known check.
tips <- c(
  sample_alignment      = "Do the count columns line up 1:1 with sample-sheet rows?",
  raw_count_sanity      = "Are values non-negative integers (raw counts, not TPM/CPM)?",
  library_size_floor    = "Hard floor on total reads per sample; below this a sample is unusable.",
  library_size_min      = "Recommended minimum total reads per sample.",
  genes_detected        = "Number of genes with >0 counts per sample.",
  replicates_per_group  = "Replicates per group in the tested factor; DE needs >=2.",
  design_identifiable   = "Is the model matrix full rank? Rank-deficient = a covariate is confounded.",
  low_count_filter      = "Fraction of genes removed by the low-count filter.",
  dispersion_fit        = "Sanity of the fitted dispersion trend.",
  cooks_outliers        = "Samples with many high Cook's-distance genes (candidate outliers)."
)
if (is.null(qc)) { cat("_QC results not found._") } else {
  n <- table(factor(qc$status, c("PASS","WARN","FAIL")))
  cat('<div class="tiles">')
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile pass"><div class="num">%d</div><div class="lab">Pass</div></div>', n["PASS"]))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile warn"><div class="num">%d</div><div class="lab">Warn</div></div>', n["WARN"]))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile fail"><div class="num">%d</div><div class="lab">Fail</div></div>', n["FAIL"]))
  cat('</div>')
  cat('<table class="qc"><tr><th>Check</th><th>Status</th><th>Value</th><th>Details</th></tr>')
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(qc))) {
    s <- qc$status[i]; chk <- qc$check[i]
    tip <- if (!is.na(tips[chk])) sprintf(' data-tip="%s"', tips[chk]) else ""
    cls <- if (nzchar(tip)) "tip" else ""
    cat(sprintf('<tr class="row-%s"><td><span class="%s"%s>%s</span></td>', s, cls, tip, chk))
    cat(sprintf('<td><span class="badge %s">%s</span></td>', s, s))
    cat(sprintf('<td>%s</td><td>%s</td></tr>',
                ifelse(is.na(qc$value[i]),"",qc$value[i]), ifelse(is.na(qc$message[i]),"",qc$message[i])))
  }
  cat('</table>')
}
```

```{r metrics, results='asis'}
                mm$metric[i], mm$value[i]))
  }

}
```

# Exploratory analysis

## PCA

Principal-component analysis of the **top `r pca_ntop`** most variable
variance-stabilized genes (configurable via `explore.pca_ntop`). Each point is a
sample; color = the tested factor, symbol = the batch variable (when present).
*Hover any point for its sample id and group; drag to zoom.*

```{r pca}
# htmlwidgets (plotly) are RETURNED as the chunk value (not cat()'d) so knitr
# attaches plotly.js into the self-contained HTML. Built via the shared helper.
pca_plotly(p_pca_tsv, p_pca_pv, p_pca)
```

**Variance explained per component (scree).** How much of the total variance each
PC captures -- the axes above show PC1 and PC2; this shows the full profile so
you can judge how many components carry real structure.

```{r scree}
pv <- if (file.exists(p_pca_pv)) as.numeric(strsplit(readLines(p_pca_pv), "\t")[[1]]) else NULL
if (have_plotly && !is.null(pv)) {
  # Drop trailing (near-)zero components for a readable axis.
  keep <- which(cumsum(pv) <= 99.9); if (length(keep) < 2) keep <- seq_len(min(length(pv), 5))
  keep <- seq_len(min(max(keep) + 1, length(pv)))
  labs <- paste0("PC", keep)
  plotly::layout(
    plotly::plot_ly(x = labs, y = pv[keep], type = "bar",
      marker = list(color = "#4f46e5"),
      text = sprintf("%.1f%%", pv[keep]), textposition = "outside",
      hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>"),
    xaxis = list(title = ""), yaxis = list(title = "% variance explained"),
    margin = list(t = 10))
} else knitr::asis_output("")
```

**How to read this plot**

- **Axes = directions of greatest variance, not biological quantities.** PC1
  captures the single largest source of variation in the data, PC2 the next
  largest (and so on). The **% variance** on each axis is how much of the total
  spread that component explains -- a high PC1 % means most of the variation is
  along one direction.
- **Distance = overall transcriptional similarity.** Samples close together have
  similar expression profiles across the top variable genes; samples far apart
  differ.
- **What "good" looks like:** samples separate by the **biological condition**
  (the color) -- ideally along PC1. That means the treatment/condition is the
  dominant signal in the data, which is what you want for a well-powered DE test.
- **Batch-effect red flag:** if samples separate by a **technical/nuisance
  variable** (the symbol -- e.g. batch, lane, donor) instead of, or on the same
  axis as, the biological condition, technical variation is competing with (or
  masking) the biology. The next two sections quantify and address this.
- **Outlier check:** a single sample sitting far from the rest on any axis is a
  candidate outlier -- cross-reference the `cooks_outliers` QC check above.
- **Caveats:** PCA is unsupervised and uses only the top variable genes, so it is
  a qualitative overview, not the DE result itself. Tight, well-separated groups
  are reassuring but not required for DESeq2 to find real differences.
- **On the gene count (`r pca_ntop`):** this is the DESeq2 `plotPCA()` default
  (500) -- a widely used convention, **not** a rigorous best practice. It is fast
  and makes results comparable across studies, but can over-weight a few very
  high-variance genes. Using more genes (1,000-2,000) gives a broader view, and
  because VST tames the mean-variance trend, running PCA on *all* genes is also
  defensible. Adjust `explore.pca_ntop` if you want a different view.

## Variance explained by metadata

Each cell is the R² of a principal component regressed on a metadata variable —
how much of that axis a variable explains. A technical variable dominating PC1
indicates a batch effect (handled inside the DE design). *Hover for exact R².*

```{r varmeta}
vm <- read_tsv_safe(p_varmeta, row.names = 1)
widget <- NULL
if (have_plotly && !is.null(vm) && ncol(vm) >= 1) {
  m <- as.matrix(vm)
  widget <- plotly::layout(
    plotly::plot_ly(x = colnames(m), y = rownames(m), z = m, type = "heatmap",
      colorscale = list(c(0,"#ffffff"), c(1,"#4f46e5")), zmin = 0, zmax = 1,
      text = matrix(sprintf("%s / %s<br>R^2 = %.2f",
              rep(rownames(m), ncol(m)), rep(colnames(m), each = nrow(m)), m), nrow = nrow(m)),
      hoverinfo = "text", colorbar = list(title = "R^2")),
    xaxis = list(title = ""), yaxis = list(title = "", autorange = "reversed"))
}
if (!is.null(widget)) widget else if (file.exists(p_vm_png)) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(p_vm_png)) else knitr::asis_output("_Not available._")
```

# Batch effects

```{r batch-intro, results='asis'}
bv <- if (nzchar(params$batch_vars)) params$batch_vars else ""
if (!nzchar(bv)) {
  cat('<p class="note">No batch / nuisance variable is present in the design ',
      '(<code>', if (!is.null(cfg)) cfg$design else "", '</code>), so no batch ',
      'correction is applicable.</p>', sep = "")
} else {
  cat(sprintf('<p>Batch / nuisance variable(s): <b>%s</b>. These are handled <b>inside the DE model</b> (design <code>%s</code>): DESeq2 estimates and removes their effect while testing the biological contrast &mdash; the raw counts are <b>never</b> modified for the statistical test.</p>',
              bv, if (!is.null(cfg)) cfg$design else ""))
  cat('<p class="note">The plot below re-runs PCA after <i>statistically subtracting</i> the batch effect (limma <code>removeBatchEffect</code>), <b>for visualization only</b>. Compare it to the PCA above: biological separation (color) should tighten and become cleaner once nuisance variation (symbol) is removed. If the two look identical, the batch variable was not contributing much; if the corrected plot separates the conditions far more cleanly, the design is correctly absorbing a real batch effect.</p>')
}
```

```{r pca-bc}
# Interactive batch-corrected PCA (same helper as the main PCA), shown only when
# a batch variable exists and its corrected scores were written.
if (nzchar(params$batch_vars) && file.exists(p_pca_bc_tsv)) {
  pca_plotly(p_pca_bc_tsv, p_pca_bc_pv, p_pca_bc)
} else {
  knitr::asis_output("")
}
```

# Differential expression

```{r de-summary, results='asis'}
de <- read_tsv_safe(p_de)
if (is.null(de)) { cat("_DE table not found._") } else {
  sig <- de$significant %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE")
  n_sig <- sum(sig, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_up   <- sum(sig & de$log2FoldChange > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_down <- sum(sig & de$log2FoldChange < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat('<div class="tiles">')
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile"><div class="num">%d</div><div class="lab">Genes tested</div></div>', nrow(de)))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile"><div class="num" style="color:%s">%d</div><div class="lab">Significant</div></div>', PAL$accent, n_sig))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile"><div class="num" style="color:%s">%d</div><div class="lab">Up in %s</div></div>', PAL$up, n_up, cfg$contrast[[2]]))
  cat(sprintf('<div class="tile"><div class="num" style="color:%s">%d</div><div class="lab">Down</div></div>', PAL$down, n_down))
  cat('</div>')
  cat(sprintf('<p class="note">Significance = padj &lt; %.3g <b>and</b> |log2FC| &ge; %.2g. Columns: <b>baseMean</b> mean normalized count; <b>log2FoldChange</b> shrunken log2(%s/%s); <b>lfcSE</b> its standard error; <b>padj</b> Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p (use this for significance).</p>',
      cfg$de$padj_cutoff, cfg$de$lfc_cutoff, cfg$contrast[[2]], cfg$contrast[[3]]))
}
```

## Volcano

*Interactive — hover any point for gene, fold-change and adjusted p; drag to zoom.*

```{r volcano}
widget <- NULL
if (have_plotly && !is.null(de)) {
  d <- de[!is.na(de$padj), ]
  if (nrow(d)) {
    d$neglog10 <- -log10(pmax(d$padj, .Machine$double.xmin))
    sig <- d$significant %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE")
    d$dir <- ifelse(sig & d$log2FoldChange > 0, "Up",
              ifelse(sig & d$log2FoldChange < 0, "Down", "n.s."))
    d$lab <- if ("symbol" %in% colnames(d)) ifelse(is.na(d$symbol) | d$symbol=="", d$gene_id, d$symbol) else d$gene_id
    d$hover <- sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>log2FC: %.2f<br>padj: %.2g", d$lab, d$log2FoldChange, d$padj)
    lfc <- cfg$de$lfc_cutoff; pcut <- -log10(cfg$de$padj_cutoff)
    line <- function(x0,x1,y0,y1) list(type="line", x0=x0,x1=x1,y0=y0,y1=y1,
        line=list(dash="dash", color="#9aa6b6", width=1))
    rng <- range(d$log2FoldChange, na.rm = TRUE)
    widget <- plotly::layout(
      plotly::plot_ly(d, x = ~log2FoldChange, y = ~neglog10, color = ~dir,
        colors = c(Up = PAL$up, Down = PAL$down, "n.s." = PAL$ns),
        text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text", type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(size = 6, opacity = 0.75)),
      xaxis = list(title = "log2 fold change"), yaxis = list(title = "-log10 adjusted p"),
      shapes = list(line(-lfc,-lfc,0,max(d$neglog10)), line(lfc,lfc,0,max(d$neglog10)),
                    line(rng[1],rng[2],pcut,pcut)))
    # Label the top genes by significance so notable hits are visible at a glance
    # (every gene is still discoverable via hover and the searchable table below).
    topn <- head(d[order(d$padj), ], 12)
    widget <- plotly::add_annotations(widget, data = topn, x = ~log2FoldChange, y = ~neglog10,
        text = ~lab, showarrow = TRUE, arrowhead = 0, arrowwidth = 0.6, arrowcolor = "#9aa6b6",
        ax = 18, ay = -14, font = list(size = 10, color = "#5b6675"))
  }
}
if (!is.null(widget)) widget else if (file.exists(p_volcano)) knitr::include_graphics(normalizePath(p_volcano)) else knitr::asis_output("_Not available._")
```

## Top genes

```{r de-table}
if (!is.null(de)) {
  cols <- intersect(c("gene_id","symbol","baseMean","log2FoldChange","lfcSE","pvalue","padj","significant"), colnames(de))
  d <- de[, cols]; numc <- vapply(d, is.numeric, logical(1))
  d[numc] <- lapply(d[numc], function(x) signif(x, 4))
  # Normalise the significance flag to the literal strings "TRUE"/"FALSE" so the
  # styleEqual() row highlight matches regardless of how read.delim typed it.
  if ("significant" %in% cols) d$significant <- ifelse(d$significant %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE"), "TRUE", "FALSE")
  if (have_DT) {
    dt <- DT::datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", extensions = "Buttons",
      class = "stripe hover row-border",
      options = list(pageLength = 15, order = list(list(which(cols=="padj")-1, "asc")),
                     dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("copy","csv"), scrollX = TRUE),
      caption = "Full DE results - search, sort, and export.")
    if ("significant" %in% cols)
      dt <- DT::formatStyle(dt, "significant", target = "row",
             backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual("TRUE", "rgba(79,70,229,.16)", default = ""),
             fontWeight = DT::styleEqual("TRUE", "600", default = "normal"))
    # Clean scientific display (3 sig figs) so tiny padj values don't show
    # floating-point artifacts like 7.3199999e-132.
    numcols <- intersect(c("baseMean","log2FoldChange","lfcSE","pvalue","padj"), cols)
    dt <- DT::formatSignif(dt, columns = numcols, digits = 3)
    htmltools::tagList(dt)
  } else knitr::kable(head(d, 25), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# Functional enrichment

```{r enrich-dot, results='asis'}
ora <- read_tsv_safe(p_ora); gsea <- read_tsv_safe(p_gsea)
if (is.null(ora) && is.null(gsea))
  cat('<p class="note">Enrichment was disabled, produced no significant terms, or was skipped (see the run log).</p>')
if (file.exists(p_dot)) cat(img_tag(p_dot, "enrichment dotplot"))
```

```{r ora-table}
if (!is.null(ora) && nrow(ora) > 0) {
  cols <- intersect(c("ID","Description","GeneRatio","p.adjust","Count"), colnames(ora))
  d <- ora[, cols]; if ("p.adjust" %in% cols) d$p.adjust <- signif(d$p.adjust, 3)
  if (have_DT) htmltools::tagList(DT::datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE), caption = "ORA - over-represented GO terms"))
  else knitr::kable(head(d, 15), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r gsea-table}
if (!is.null(gsea) && nrow(gsea) > 0) {
  cols <- intersect(c("ID","Description","setSize","NES","p.adjust"), colnames(gsea))
  d <- gsea[, cols]; numc <- vapply(d, is.numeric, logical(1)); d[numc] <- lapply(d[numc], signif, 3)
  if (have_DT) htmltools::tagList(DT::datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE), caption = "GSEA - enriched gene sets"))
  else knitr::kable(head(d, 15), row.names = FALSE)
}
```
